posts.author: Canned_Dinosaur
posts.body:
Okay, so there might be some confusion in what you and I mean with "already implemented", so let's just assume that nothing is implemented yet. A couple of things to consider:
By default you have three gauges at your disposal to customize (and I honestly don't know if you can add more within the confines of Visustella). Showing special gauges is essentially replacing HP/MP/TP gauges with one of the customized ones. As the gauge replacement can only be set by class, and as there is no way to change the gauge replacements on the fly through plugin commands, you need to make conscious choices on how to implement this.
Next, you have actually two things to keep track of: number of bullets in inventory, and number of bullets in your firearm. The cost is based off of the latter, and the reload action will replace bullets in your firearm with bullets from your inventory. How you need to implement this can get complicated depending on what you want:
Do you have multiple actors that can have this class?
Do you have multiple weapons of each type for which you need to keep track of number of bullets in the gun?
It's probably better to focus on implementing this mechanic first, and worry about the esthetics later.
What you need to do:
Have a skill to fire each fire arm
Decide on a note tag to specify the special cost of the skill, for example
<BULLETA COST: 1>
and
<BULLETB COST: 1>
Create entries under
Skill Cost Types
for Bullet A (for Bullet B it's easier to copy Bullet A after we are finished). Just copy the entry for
Potion
and change the value under
Name
to
Bullet A
or something.
If you can tell us the item ID of the bullet items, we can tell you where you need to tweak what.

I think multiple characters is doable by having bullets in the gun as a variable, and a stock of bullets as an item (with no maximum). per

posts.author: rpgLord69
posts.body:
@Angy1910
Yeah Skill and States Core, Skill Cost Type settings. But MP is already set up there, so you just need to modify it. Remove the draw gauge stuff from there and add similar stuff there to what I posted on the previous page. But instead of checking for items, just loop from 1 to user.mp to add the icons. Make it change the line by adding to target y after every 5 or whatever icons. Also delete the other loop that was adding icons for empty chambers in the ammo system. You can also use the replace gauge notetag to get rid of the tp gauge (whilst still leaving more area on the box).
The only problem is that it might fit 2-3 rows (depending on your icon size), but even with the tp gauge set to 'none', it still cuts off somewhere around where it's supposed to be, so you can't use the whole area for your mp crystals. I tested it earlier and trying to resize the mp gauge bitmap height didn't seem to help with the cutoff. And like I said, I'm not an expert with those draw areas. But there are many people here who could probably answer how to claim the bottom area too for the mp gauge.
If you don't want to use VS, check the placeBasicGauges, placeGauge and Sprite_Gauge to check if you can use that same blt icon stuff from previous page when it draws your mp type gauge.
